ModMetadata.Name: IZCode
ModMetadata.Author: julianobd
ModMetadata.Description:
[h1]IZCode - Structured Programming for Stationeers[/h1]
IZCode replaces IC10 with IZ: a structured language with types, real functions and recursion, on its own virtual machine inside the Programmable Chip.
Write [b]#iz[/b] on the first line of a chip and IZCode takes over. Chips without the marker keep running as IC10, so existing builds are unaffected.
[h2]WHY IT EXISTS[/h2]
[table] [tr][th]IC10[/th][th]IZ[/th][/tr] [tr][td]128 lines, 4096 bytes[/td][td]2000 lines, 16000 bytes[/td][/tr] [tr][td]16 registers[/td][td]Named variables managed by the compiler[/td][/tr] [tr][td]jal/ra, limited calls[/td][td]Functions, parameters, returns and recursion[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Restarts every tick[/td][td]Freezes and resumes execution[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Infinite loop hangs the chip[/td][td]VM preempts execution automatically[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Typos found at runtime[/td][td]Compile errors with suggestions[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Everything is a double[/td][td]num, bool, str and dev are type-checked[/td][/tr] [tr][td]HASH("text")[/td][td]Real strings with concatenation and comparison[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Loose registers[/td][td]Arrays, structs and lists[/td][/tr] [/table]
[h2]A COMPLETE PROGRAM[/h2]
[code] #iz device sensor = d0; device inlet = d1;
const TARGET = 101.325;
fn main() { loop { var p = sensor.Pressure; inlet.On = p < TARGET - 5.0; yield; } } [/code]
Execution starts at [b]fn main()[/b]. When it returns, the chip stops until restarted.
[h2]THE LANGUAGE[/h2]
[h3]Types[/h3]
[list] [*][b]num[/b] — 64-bit floating-point number [*][b]bool[/b] — Boolean value [*][b]str[/b] — Immutable ASCII string [*][b]dev[/b] — Device pin d0-d5, or db [*][b]T[N][/b] — Fixed-size arrays [*][b]list[/b] — Typed collections [*][b]struct[/b] — User-defined structures [/list]
num and bool are not interchangeable: [b]if x[/b] needs a bool; write [b]if x != 0[/b] for a number.
[code] var counter = 0; var active: bool = false; const MAX = 101.325; [/code]
Globals keep their values across ticks.
[h3]Arrays and Structs[/h3]
Arrays and structs live in the VM heap, laid out at compile time. No allocator, no GC.
[code] var samples: num[8];
struct Gauge { total: num; cursor: num; samples: num[8]; } [/code]
Array length is part of the type; [b]len(a)[/b] is compile-time. Aggregates pass by reference.
[h3]Lists and Queries[/h3]
Fixed-size arrays with a count, and LINQ-style queries:
[code] var rooms: list Room[8];
var r: Room; r.temp = 40; rooms.add(r);
var mean = rooms.avg(x => x.temp); var hot = rooms.where(x => x.temp > 30); var worst = rooms.orderByDesc(x => x.temp).first(); [/code]
[b]Queries:[/b]
[list] [*]where, select, take, skip [*]takeWhile, skipWhile [*]orderBy, orderByDesc, reverse [*]distinct, sum, avg, min, max [*]count, any, all [*]first, last, firstOr, lastOr [*]contains, indexOf, into [/list]
A query chain becomes a single loop, with the lambdas inlined: no intermediate lists, no per-element calls.
[h3]Devices[/h3]
Device properties are checked against the game's LogicType table:
[code] var p = sensor.Pressure; pump.On = true; [/code]
Invalid properties are compile errors: [b]Presure[/b] answers [i]did you mean Pressure?[/i]
[b]db[/b] is the device the chip is installed in, and the only way to reach it: nothing can be wired to it. In a circuit housing it is the housing; in a hardsuit it is the suit, so a program can read its own PressureExternal and drive its AC. On a suit the pins are the wearer's slots: d0 helmet, d1 backpack, d2 toolbelt, d3 glasses, d4 and d5 hands.
[code] device self = db; self.Setting = 1; [/code]
[b]isset(dev)[/b] tells whether a pin has a device on it right now, so a program drives whatever is there instead of stopping on an empty pin. IC10's [b]sdse[/b].
[code] device helmet = d0;
if isset(helmet) { helmet.On = true; } [/code]
[h3]Game Constants[/h3]
The game's named values, spelled as IC10 spells them:
[code] light.Color = Color.Green; cooler.Mode = AirCon.Cold; [/code]
All 30 groups come from the game itself: Color, GasType, SlotClass, Sound, AirCon, PowerMode, EntityState, LogicType and the rest. Each value folds to its number at compile time, and a typo is a compile error with the nearest name.
[h3]Batch Operations[/h3]
Every matching device on the network:
[code] all(StructureWallLight).On = true; named("Corridor Light").On = false; named(StructureVolumePump, "north").On = true;
var avg = all(StructureGasSensor).Pressure; var total = all(StructureSolarPanel).PowerGeneration.sum(); [/code]
A bare read averages; [b]sum()[/b], [b]min()[/b], [b]max()[/b] and [b]count()[/b] collapse it another way.
A selector can be named and then used like a device on a pin:
[code] device led = named(StructureDiode, #"led-dev"); led.On = true; [/code]
Prefab names, [b]#"hash"[/b] literals and constants cost nothing at runtime.
[h3]Text[/h3]
Strings are real runtime values: variables, parameters, returns, arrays and structs.
[code] var label = "vent-" + side; all("Structure" + kind).On = true; [/code]
[b]Functions:[/b] [b]len[/b], [b]hash[/b], [b]char[/b], [b]chr[/b], [b]sub[/b], [b]find[/b], [b]text[/b], [b]fixed[/b], [b]parse[/b].
Numbers become text only through [b]text(x)[/b].
[h3]Control Flow[/h3]
[list] [*]if / else if / else [*]while / loop [*]for [*]break / continue [/list]
Ranges support [b]0..10[/b] and [b]0..=10[/b]. There is no goto or labels. Braces are mandatory.
[h3]Functions and Recursion[/h3]
Functions have typed parameters, return values and recursion.
[code] fn gcd(a: num, b: num) -> num { if b == 0 { return a; } return gcd(b, a % b); } [/code]
A call-depth limit turns runaway recursion into a clean error.
[h3]Operators and Math[/h3]
Operators follow C precedence. Prefix: [b]-x[/b], [b]!x[/b] and [b]~x[/b].
Division by zero follows IEEE-754. Assignment is a statement, so [b]if (a = b)[/b] does not compile.
Math and trigonometry are there too, plus [b]rand[/b], [b]nan[/b] and [b]inf[/b].
[h3]Tick Control[/h3]
[b]yield[/b] gives the tick back and resumes at the next instruction.
[b]sleep(2)[/b] suspends execution.
Without either, the VM preempts when the budget ends.
[h2]THE EDITOR, UPGRADED[/h2]
[h3]Real Code Area[/h3]
IZ mode replaces the editor's 128 text fields with one real editor, with a gutter and current-line highlight.
[list] [*]Drag selection [*]Shift + Arrow [*]Ctrl + A / C / X / V [*]Mouse wheel [*]VS Code-style indentation [/list]
[h3]Wiring-Aware Completion[/h3]
The editor knows what is on each pin, and what a selector reaches: [b]pump.[/b] and [b]leds.[/b] suggest that device's properties, with live values.
It also completes pins, prefabs, slot properties, game constants, queries and your own declarations.
[h3]Live Errors[/h3]
The compiler the chip runs analyzes the editor as you type.
[list] [*]Red underline — errors [*]Amber underline — warnings [*]Diagnostic panel with details [/list]
Runtime errors light the housing's error LED, as an IC10 exception does.
[h3]Hover Information[/h3]
Hover a device to see its equipment, label, hash and readable properties.
[h2]REQUIREMENTS[/h2]
IZCode is a C# plugin, so it needs a mod loader.
[list] [*]BepInEx [*][url=https://github.com/StationeersLaunchPad/StationeersLaunchPad]StationeersLaunchPad[/url] [/list]
Enable IZCode in the mods menu; [b][IZCode][/b] in [b]Player.log[/b] confirms it loaded.
[h2]SAFE TO TRY[/h2]
[b]#iz[/b] is a valid IC10 comment, so an IZ chip does not break for players without IZCode.
Example programs are in [b]samples/[/b]: pressure, solar tracking, queries and a hardsuit controller.
[h2]MULTIPLAYER[/h2]
[b]Multiplayer has NOT been tested.[/b]
Every client and the server need the mod installed.
[h2]LINKS[/h2]
[b]Source code:[/b] [url=https://github.com/julianobd/IZCode]GitHub Repository[/url]
[b]Bug reports:[/b] [url=https://github.com/julianobd/IZCode/issues]Issue Tracker[/url]
[hr]
[i]IZCode - Structured programming for Stationeers.[/i]
ModMetadata.ChangeLog:
===== 0.1.6 =========================================================
- Added 'isset(dev)', which answers whether a pin has a device on it right now. A program can drive whatever is wired instead of stopping on an empty pin: the suit script that only touches the helmet when one is worn, the routine over six optional pins. It takes a device declared with 'device', a pin written straight into the call - 'isset(d3)' - and 'db', the device the chip is installed in; a name standing for 'all(...)' or 'named(...)' reaches a set rather than a pin and is refused at compile time. Reading an empty pin still stops the program and lights the housing LED, which is the right answer for a cable somebody will plug in. This is IC10's 'sdse'. See 'samples/optional-devices.iz'.
- Batch reads now answer in the five modes the game has, not only the average. A batch property is the sequence of readings of every device the selector matched, and used bare it still means '.avg()'; written after it, 'sum()', 'min()', 'max()' and 'count()' collapse that sequence another way. They work on the inline selector and on a name declared from one - 'all(X).Power.sum()' and 'panels.Charge.min()' - take no argument, and pick which of the game's batch methods travels in the instruction, so the chain costs the single read the bare property costs. An empty batch gives 0 for all of them, 'min()' included, which is 0 and not infinity; 'count()' is the one that still answers, and it is what tells "nothing on the network" from "everything reading zero". The editor offers the five after 'all(X).Power.', and hovering the chain shows the value under the mode that was written. See 'samples/solar.iz'.
